subject.title: iOS app: push notifications for assistant messages + background Talk mode

question: Should native iOS assistant-message notifications ship as generic privacy-safe alerts first, allow opt-in transcript previews, or remain unsupported until a broader mobile notification/background-audio policy is approved?
rationale: The APNs registration, relay, local notification, and exec-approval push pieces exist, but payload content, lock-screen privacy, tap routing, duplicate-foreground behavior, per-device opt-in semantics, and background microphone behavior require maintainer product/security intent.

options.title: Approve generic alerts first
options.body: Add a dedicated assistant-message APNs kind and iOS tap route with generic notification content by default, leaving transcript previews for a later explicit opt-in.

options.title: Allow explicit transcript previews
options.body: Permit assistant reply text in APNs only behind a visible per-device or per-gateway privacy setting with tests and docs for relay and lock-screen behavior.

options.title: Defer native chat pushes
options.body: Keep relying on foreground iOS state and third-party channels until maintainers define a broader mobile notification and background Talk policy.

recommendation.title: Approve generic alerts first
recommendation.body: Add a dedicated assistant-message APNs kind and iOS tap route with generic notification content by default, leaving transcript previews for a later explicit opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available routing candidate from the likely-owner set for the iOS/Gateway product and privacy decision.
